title: infer meiotic phase and consequence from chromosome behavior
stem: A diploid cell has completed DNA replication. In a micrograph, homologous chromosomes are paired at the cell equator, and the two sister chromatids of each chromosome remain attached. If the spindle pulls each homolog toward a different pole, which event and immediate outcome are shown?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metaphase II followed by separation of sister chromatids; each resulting cell has both homologs.
choices.rationale: Meiosis II begins with no homologous pairs in one cell; sisters separate there, not paired homologs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metaphase I followed by separation of homologs; each resulting cell has one replicated chromosome from each pair.
choices.rationale: Correct: Paired homologs at one plate identify meiosis I. Anaphase I moves homologs, not sisters, yielding two haploid cells whose chromosomes remain replicated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitosis followed by separation of homologs; each resulting cell has half the original chromosome number.
choices.rationale: Mitosis separates sister chromatids and maintains chromosome number per daughter cell.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Anaphase II followed by separation of homologs; each resulting cell has two chromatids from every pair.
choices.rationale: Anaphase II separates sisters after homologs were divided in meiosis I; it does not retain two chromatids per resulting chromosome.

title: infer meiotic phase and consequence from chromosome behavior (variant 1)
stem: A researcher marks the centromere of each sister chromatid in one diploid cell. After the first cytokinesis, two cells contain one homolog from each original pair, but each chromosome still consists of two attached chromatids. Which next step directly creates four cells with one chromatid per chromosome?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pairing of homologs during prophase I, followed by the first cytokinesis.
choices.rationale: Homolog pairing precedes the first division and cannot convert the observed two cells into four cells with single chromatids.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Separation of homologs during anaphase I, followed by the second cytokinesis.
choices.rationale: Homologs have already separated; repeating that step would not split attached sister chromatids.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Another round of DNA replication, followed by chromosome separation in mitosis.
choices.rationale: Meiosis II has no intervening DNA replication; replication would add rather than remove attached chromatids.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separation of sister chromatids during anaphase II, followed by the second cytokinesis.
choices.rationale: Correct: The observed two cells are after meiosis I. Meiosis II separates attached sisters and the second cytokinesis yields four haploid cells.

title: infer meiotic phase and consequence from chromosome behavior (variant 2)
stem: In a cell from a sexually reproducing diploid organism, spindle fibers pull the two sister chromatids of each chromosome toward opposite poles. The cell already contains only one member of each homologous pair. Which interpretation fits both observations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cell is in anaphase II; homologs separated in the previous division and sister chromatids are now separating.
choices.rationale: Correct: One homolog per pair indicates the reductional division has occurred; active sister separation is anaphase II.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cell is in anaphase I; homologous pairs are being pulled apart for the first time.
choices.rationale: Anaphase I moves homologs while sister centromeres remain attached.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cell is in metaphase I; homologous pairs are aligned but no chromosomes are moving.
choices.rationale: Metaphase I aligns paired homologs in a diploid cell and does not pull sisters apart.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cell is in mitosis; its two daughters will necessarily be diploid like the original parent cell.
choices.rationale: Mitosis also separates sisters, but this cell is already haploid after the first meiotic division, so diploid daughters do not follow.

title: infer meiotic phase and consequence from chromosome behavior (variant 3)
stem: Four nuclei form after a diploid germ cell divides twice, with DNA replicated only before the first division. In the first division, sister chromatids stay together while homologs separate. Which description of the second division is consistent with the final four nuclei?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The original diploid cell separates homologs again, producing four diploid nuclei with replicated chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Homolog separation has already occurred and the original cell no longer exists after the first division.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each haploid cell replicates DNA again and then separates homologous pairs, producing four diploid nuclei.
choices.rationale: No replication occurs between meiotic divisions, and each haploid cell has only one homolog per pair.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each of the two haploid cells separates sister chromatids, producing four haploid nuclei with unduplicated chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Correct: Meiosis I reduces homolog number in each cell; without another replication, meiosis II separates sisters and produces four haploid nuclei.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two haploid cells fuse before separating sister chromatids, producing four genetically identical diploid nuclei.
choices.rationale: Fusion would restore diploidy and is not part of the second meiotic division.

title: track chromosome and chromatid counts across divisions
stem: A germ cell has 2n=6 chromosomes. DNA replicates once before meiosis, and no chromosomes are lost. Immediately after meiosis I, what does each of the two cells contain, and what will each contain after meiosis II? Count a chromosome by its centromere.

choices.label: A
choices.text: After meiosis I: 6 chromosomes and 6 chromatids; after meiosis II: 3 chromosomes and 3 chromatids.
choices.rationale: This counts both post-I cells together rather than each one; one post-I cell has only three centromeres.

choices.label: B
choices.text: After meiosis I: 3 chromosomes and 6 chromatids; after meiosis II: 3 chromosomes and 3 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Correct: Homolog separation halves chromosome number from 6 to 3 but keeps sisters joined (6 chromatids). Sister separation yields 3 unduplicated chromosomes per gamete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: After meiosis I: 3 chromosomes and 3 chromatids; after meiosis II: 3 chromosomes and 6 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Meiosis I does not separate sisters, and meiosis II does not replicate DNA.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After meiosis I: 6 chromosomes and 12 chromatids; after meiosis II: 6 chromosomes and 6 chromatids.
choices.rationale: This retains the diploid chromosome number in every product despite homolog separation.

title: track chromosome and chromatid counts across divisions (variant 1)
stem: A diploid organism has 2n=8. A student counts chromosomes by centromeres and measures DNA as chromatids. Compare one cell at metaphase I with one cell at metaphase II, assuming normal separation and no additional replication. Which pair of counts is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metaphase I: 8 chromosomes, 16 chromatids; metaphase II: 4 chromosomes, 8 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Correct: Replication doubles chromatids, not centromeres. Meiosis I halves centromeres per cell but leaves each chromosome duplicated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metaphase I: 16 chromosomes, 16 chromatids; metaphase II: 8 chromosomes, 8 chromatids.
choices.rationale: This treats each chromatid as a chromosome at metaphase I and fails to account for attached sisters at metaphase II.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metaphase I: 8 chromosomes, 8 chromatids; metaphase II: 4 chromosomes, 4 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Both metaphase stages occur before sister separation, so each chromosome has two chromatids.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metaphase I: 8 chromosomes, 16 chromatids; metaphase II: 8 chromosomes, 16 chromatids.
choices.rationale: The first division separates homologs; a metaphase-II cell is haploid, with four chromosomes rather than eight.

title: track chromosome and chromatid counts across divisions (variant 2)
stem: A diploid cell with 2n=10 enters meiosis after DNA replication. A technician counts five chromosomes per cell immediately after the first division. If the second division proceeds normally, which count and cell number should the technician record at the end?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Four cells, each with ten chromosomes containing one chromatid each.
choices.rationale: Meiosis II does not restore the original diploid chromosome count per cell.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Four cells, each with five chromosomes containing one chromatid each.
choices.rationale: Correct: Meiosis I produces two haploid cells with five duplicated chromosomes each; meiosis II separates sisters, making four cells with five unduplicated chromosomes each.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two cells, each with five chromosomes containing two chromatids each.
choices.rationale: This describes the state after meiosis I, not the end of meiosis II.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Four cells, each with five chromosomes containing two chromatids each.
choices.rationale: Sister chromatids separate during meiosis II, so the final chromosomes each have one chromatid.

title: track chromosome and chromatid counts across divisions (variant 3)
stem: A diploid plant has 2n=12. A premeiotic cell has completed S phase. Its four final meiotic products are analyzed separately. Assuming normal meiosis, which change in chromosome and chromatid count occurs from the premeiotic cell to any one final product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From 12 chromosomes/24 chromatids to 6 chromosomes/6 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Correct: S phase duplicates chromatids without changing 12 centromeres; meiosis I halves homolog count, and meiosis II separates sisters, leaving six single-chromatid chromosomes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From 24 chromosomes/24 chromatids to 12 chromosomes/12 chromatids.
choices.rationale: A replicated chromatid is not a separate chromosome while sisters share a centromere; each gamete is haploid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From 12 chromosomes/12 chromatids to 6 chromosomes/12 chromatids.
choices.rationale: The premeiotic cell has already undergone S phase, and final gametes have separated sister chromatids.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From 12 chromosomes/24 chromatids to 12 chromosomes/12 chromatids.
choices.rationale: Final meiotic products have half the original chromosome count, not the diploid count.

title: compare mitosis and meiosis using observed products
stem: A diploid cell line is filmed through division. In trial X, paired homologs align at one plate; after two divisions there are four haploid cells. In trial Y, individual duplicated chromosomes align; after one division there are two diploid cells. Which inference best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: X is mitosis because homolog pairing yields identical daughters; Y is meiosis because one division makes diploid gametes.
choices.rationale: Homolog pairing is characteristic of meiosis I, and mitosis does not make four haploid products.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both are meiosis because every division uses a spindle; the number of products depends only on cell size.
choices.rationale: Both use spindles, but spindle use alone does not explain reductional versus equational outcomes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: X is meiosis because homologs segregate before sisters; Y is mitosis because sisters segregate in one division without reducing ploidy.
choices.rationale: Correct: Paired homolog alignment and reduction plus a second division diagnose meiosis; one sister-separation division preserving ploidy diagnoses mitosis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both are mitosis because chromosomes align at a plate in each trial.
choices.rationale: Alignment occurs in both processes, but homolog pairing and product ploidy distinguish them.

title: compare mitosis and meiosis using observed products (variant 1)
stem: A researcher disables a protein needed to keep sister centromeres joined through the first division of meiosis. In a normal control, homologs separate first and sisters separate in the second division. What observation would most directly reveal that the mutant failed to follow the normal meiotic sequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Homologous chromosomes pair during prophase I before they separate.
choices.rationale: Homolog pairing is an expected normal event and does not reveal loss of sister cohesion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two haploid cells are present after the first cytokinesis, each with duplicated chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Attached sisters after meiosis I indicate the protein's role was maintained, not lost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Four haploid cells are present after two divisions, each with unduplicated chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Four unduplicated haploid products describe the normal endpoint and do not directly show premature sister separation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sister chromatids separate during the first division instead of remaining attached while homologs move apart.
choices.rationale: Correct: The protein's specified role is sister cohesion in meiosis I; losing it permits premature sister separation, violating the observed order.

title: compare mitosis and meiosis using observed products (variant 2)
stem: A diploid parent cell makes two daughter cells in culture. Each daughter has the same number of chromosome sets as the parent and received one chromatid from each replicated chromosome. A separate germ cell makes four cells, each with one chromosome set. Which event explains the set-number difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cultured cell separated homologs in mitosis, whereas the germ cell separated sisters in meiosis I.
choices.rationale: Mitosis segregates sisters; meiosis I segregates homologs, the reverse of this choice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The germ cell replicated DNA between its two divisions, restoring two chromosome sets in each product.
choices.rationale: No S phase occurs between meiosis I and II, and replication would not explain haploid products.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cultured cell paired homologs and crossed them over, while the germ cell skipped chromosome separation.
choices.rationale: Meiotic products require chromosome separation; homolog pairing is associated with meiosis I, not ordinary mitosis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The germ cell separated homologous chromosomes in its first division, whereas the cultured cell separated sister chromatids in a single mitotic division.
choices.rationale: Correct: Homolog segregation reduces chromosome sets in meiosis I; sister segregation alone in mitosis preserves the original set number.

title: compare mitosis and meiosis using observed products (variant 3)
stem: A microscopy study compares two divisions of the same germ-cell lineage. After division 1, each cell has one homolog from every pair but its sister chromatids are still joined. After division 2, sister chromatids are separate. Why can division 2 occur without another S phase and still produce gametes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Division 1 has already separated sister chromatids, so division 2 only replicates the homologs.
choices.rationale: The observation explicitly says sisters remain joined after division 1; replication is not division 2's role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each post-division-1 cell is diploid, so division 2 must remove an entire homolog pair from each cell.
choices.rationale: One homolog per pair means the post-I cells are haploid, and meiosis II separates sisters rather than homolog pairs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each chromosome already has two chromatids after division 1, so division 2 partitions those sisters into haploid cells with unduplicated chromosomes.
choices.rationale: Correct: Meiosis I leaves sisters attached in haploid cells. Meiosis II distributes existing chromatids; no new DNA synthesis is required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gametes are made by fusing the two cells from division 1 before division 2 begins.
choices.rationale: Cell fusion would restore diploidy and is not part of meiosis II.
